name: Range interval with point estimate
reader_question: What range does the source state for each item, and where does its point estimate sit?
relationship: Per-item stated low–high range with a point estimate inside it, on one zero-based scale.
use_when: A source states a low, a high and a point value for each item
The width of the stated range is part of the finding
avoid_when: The range is a statistical confidence interval derived from a sample — use a distribution form
Only point values exist — use ranked-bar

data_contract.notes: Upper axis bound; defaults to a rounded value above the largest high
Stated figures; must satisfy low ≤ point ≤ high

units: One unit throughout; the scale starts at zero.

editable: Range bars, point markers and labels as native shapes and text
not_data_bound: Range and marker geometry is drawn on a computed scale; values are not data-bound and there is no embedded workbook
Editing a figure means resizing the bar, moving the marker and rewriting its labels

table_alternative: A table of item, low, point estimate and high.
variations: Ranges with an overlaid reference line
Ranges at two cut-offs on separate rows
limitations: The range is whatever the source states; it carries no probability
Overlapping ranges do not establish a ranking

excluded_alternatives.form: Error bars on a bar chart
excluded_alternatives.reason: Suggest a statistical interval around a measured mean that the source does not provide
Implies a forecast distribution over time
